subStages.question: Fill in the missing word
subStages.prompt: Long ago in ancient Rome, salt was so valuable that it was sometimes used to pay people. A soldier's salt allowance was called his salarium, which is where our modern word "salary" comes from. If a worker did a poor job, people felt he had not earned the salt he was being paid. Today, when someone is not good enough at what they do, we say they are "not worth their {{b1}}."

blanks.hint: It is the precious white mineral mentioned throughout the clue.

feedback.correct: Correct! Someone who is not worth their salt is not considered good enough at their job.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Think of the precious white mineral that was once used as payment.

subStages.question: Fill in the missing word
subStages.prompt: Salt has long been associated with saving and protecting things because it can keep food from spoiling. This connection between salt and saving also influenced religious language. The word for the saving of a person's soul is called {{b1}}.

blanks.hint: This word means the saving of a person's soul.

feedback.correct: Correct! Salvation means being saved, especially in a religious sense.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Think of the religious word for the saving of a person's soul.

subStages.question: Fill in the missing phrase
subStages.prompt: The ancient Roman writer Pliny the Elder wrote about medicine that was taken with a small pinch of salt. Over time, this became a way of saying that you should be a little doubtful when hearing something hard to believe. When you should not believe something completely, you should {{b1}}.

blanks.answer: take it with a grain of salt
blanks.hint: The phrase tells you to add a tiny amount of doubt, like adding a tiny amount of salt.

feedback.correct: Correct! To take something with a grain of salt means to be slightly skeptical about it.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Think of the expression that tells you to be a little skeptical.

subStages.question: Fill in the missing word
subStages.prompt: In the periodic table, some elements are grouped together because they behave in similar ways. Group 17 contains elements such as chlorine, fluorine, and iodine. The group's name comes from Greek words meaning "salt-producing." This group of elements is called the {{b1}} family.

blanks.hint: This is the name of the group 17 family that includes chlorine and fluorine.

feedback.correct: Correct! The halogen family is group 17 of the periodic table.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Think of the group 17 family that includes chlorine, fluorine, and iodine.

subStages.question: Fill in the missing word
subStages.prompt: Very salty water can create a sharp, stinging feeling on your skin, eyes, or lips. Salt water used for preserving foods such as pickles has a special name. This very salty preserving liquid is called {{b1}}.

blanks.hint: It is the salty liquid commonly used to preserve pickles and other foods.

feedback.correct: Correct! Brine is salty water used for preserving food.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Think of the salty liquid used to preserve pickles.

subStages.question: Fill in the missing phrase
subStages.prompt: In medieval England, a valuable salt container was placed in the middle of a large dinner table. Important guests sat close to the salt, while lower-ranking guests sat farther away. Someone seated in the honored position was said to be {{b1}}.

blanks.hint: Important guests sat closer to the salt, so they were described as being higher than it.

feedback.correct: Correct! Being "above the salt" meant occupying an honored position at the table.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Important guests sat closer to the salt and were said to be what the salt?

subStages.question: Fill in the missing phrase
subStages.prompt: In Russia and other Slavic countries, an important guest may be welcomed with a decorated loaf of bread and a dish of salt. The guest takes some bread, dips it in the salt, and eats it as a sign of friendship and trust. This traditional ceremony is known as a {{b1}} welcome.

blanks.hint: Think of the two foods traditionally offered to an honored guest.

feedback.correct: Correct! Bread and salt are traditional symbols of hospitality and friendship.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Think of the two foods offered together to welcome an honored guest.

subStages.question: Put the events in chronological order
subStages.instructions: Drag each historical event to its correct place on the timeline.

events.title: Romanian Salt Springs
events.description: People living in what is now Romania boiled water from natural salt springs to collect salt. This is one of the oldest known salt-making sites in the world.

events.title: Solnitsata Salt Center
events.description: At Solnitsata in present-day Bulgaria, people produced salt by boiling brine. The settlement later became one of Europe's earliest known towns.

events.title: Salt in Egyptian Tombs
events.description: Ancient Egyptians placed salt, salted birds and fish inside tombs as valuable funeral offerings.

events.title: Egyptian Salt Trade
events.description: Egypt exported salted fish to the Phoenicians in exchange for cedar wood, glass and the famous Tyrian purple dye.

learning.message: Salt draws moisture out of food. Reducing moisture helps preserve food, which is why salt has long been used when curing meat.

subStages.question: Colors with Real Stories
subStages.prompt: When you finish this world, keep exploring the hidden colors around you.

clues.clue1: It takes about 150,000 hand-picked, dried crocus flowers to produce just 1 kilogram of this dye.
clues.hint: For most of history this dye traded at nearly the same value as gold and silver by weight. Only three stigmas can be hand-plucked per flower, which is why the price has never really dropped.
clues.name: Saffron

clues.clue1: A dye-maker in 1704 was trying to invent a red pigment from crushed cochineal insects but accidentally created this instead.
clues.hint: The resulting compound is now an FDA-approved antidote for radioactive cesium and thallium poisoning, kept in nuclear emergency kits worldwide. It also gave photography the cyanotype process, the original technique behind architectural blueprints.
clues.name: Prussian Blue

clues.clue1: Dye-makers had to crack open roughly 12,000 sea snails to extract enough gland fluid to color a single garment hem.
clues.hint: In 2024, Paris Olympics organizers chose this exact hue for the running track at the Stade de France, the first time in Olympic history the surface was not red or blue.
clues.name: Tyrian Purple

clues.clue1: In 2023, scientists found that many walls at this ancient Roman site were never actually painted this color — it appeared by accident.
clues.hint: Lab analysis showed the original pigment was yellow ochre, chemically transformed in moments by superheated volcanic gas during the 79 CE eruption.
clues.name: Pompeian Red

feedback.correct: Every color found its story. Great eye!
feedback.incorrect: Not quite — try again and watch for the small details.

nodes.mapSubtitle: Explore the root SALT and discover words that originated from it.

clues.title: Salted herbs
clues.text: Romans ate vegetables and herbs preserved in salt. This practice gave rise to the word SALAD — from the Latin 'salata,' meaning salted.

clues.title: Soldiers' allowance
clues.text: Roman soldiers received a monthly allowance called SALARIUM, used to buy salt. This is the origin of the modern English word SALARY.

clues.title: French condiment
clues.text: In French, SAUCE originally meant salted food. The word evolved to describe savory liquid preparations served alongside meals.

clues.title: Things preserved in salt
clues.text: Sausage comes from the Latin SALSUS, meaning salted. Meat was preserved by packing it in salt — the origin of SALAMI and SAUSAGE.

clues.title: Spanish sauce
clues.text: SALSA literally means 'sauce' in Spanish. The term described spicy, salt-based tomato condiments in Mexican cooking.

clues.title: Saline solution
clues.text: SALINE — a solution of salt in water — takes its name directly from Latin SAL. Used in medicine for wound washing and injections.
